name: The Goods
blocked: Confirmed via the Clover COLO2 RSC-payload technique (curl + probe/extract_clover_colo2.js) that this is a closed-store price gate, not a JS-rendering wall: the payload parses cleanly but the catalog itself is filtered down to only 3 priced items (Brown Butter Donut $5.00, Espresso $4.00, Cortado 4oz $4.25) out of a normal ~20 doughnut flavours plus drinks - the same collapse-to-a-few-items signature documented for this exact restaurant previously. Store hours are ~8:00am-2:00pm; capture was attempted at ~00:15 Pacific (well outside trading hours), and --with-required-modifiers found no additional recoverable prices.
notes: Needs a daytime (8am-2pm Pacific) retry, not a browser - the COLO2 extraction path itself now works fine on this storefront.

name: Cotijas Taco Shop
blocked: No usable priced source found for this exact address (17090 Bernardo Center Dr #124). Website is null and no live domain found for this specific location (the chain's other domains - thecotijastacoshop.com/cotijasmarkest, cotijastacoshopca.com, ordercotijastacoshop{bonita,chulavista}.com - list only their own 2-4 locations each, none of which is Bernardo Center). Grubhub, Seamless and UberEats pages for this store are pure JS shells that returned nothing to curl. Yelp's biz page is bot-blocked; Yelp's dedicated MENU TAB exists (yelp.com/menu/cotijas-taco-shop-san-diego-14) but is barred by house rule regardless. restaurantji.com hosts a dine-in menu-board photo for this location (cdn6.localdatacdn.com/images/3413166/d_cotija_s_taco_shop_menu.jpg) but only as a low-resolution 4-panel collage: two panels are legible (a specialty/add-on burrito list at $9.49-$11.79, a Combos board #1-6 at $12.49, Daily/Weekly Specials board with Taco Tuesday $1.89, Baja Wednesday fish taco $2, Thursday 5 rolled tacos $4.59, Friday potato taco $1.89, Saturday/Sunday combos $8.99), but the other two panels - which show the core Burritos, Tacos, Bowls or Shells and Quesadillas boards in a wide establishing shot - are too small in this collage to read any item or price. No higher-resolution version of those two panels was reachable (restaurantji's per-photo gallery route did not serve a static image to curl, and direct id-based CDN URLs 404'd).
notes: Recording blocked rather than a partial: what is legible is combos/specials, not the core burrito/taco/bowl/quesadilla menu, so filing it would misrepresent the shape of the menu. A Chrome-equipped agent could likely finish this in one pass by opening restaurantji's photo gallery (or Yelp's full photo set) and reading the individual full-resolution board photos.

name: George Burgers
blocked: restaurantguru.com's 'owner' menu (used in a prior pass) is a directory source that the screener now rejects without an independent priced cross-check, so I tried to corroborate it against DoorDash's JSON-LD (schema.org Menu, server-side, 91 items - the same dataset a documented prior finding flagged as dividing cleanly by 1.20 for a uniform delivery markup; confirmed again here: 79/91 land on round dollars after /1.20). The two do not agree, even accounting for the known 1.20 markup: e.g. restaurantguru's Grilled Chicken Sandwich $9.14 vs DoorDash's own base price (($6.00 displayed)/1.20=$5.00); Fish Sandwich $8.57 vs $5.00 base; BLT $9.14 vs $4.00 base; 1/4 Burger Combo $16.99 vs the equivalent combo's $9.00 base - ratios of 1.6x-2.3x with no consistent multiplier, which is a staleness/mismatch signal rather than a markup relationship. Website is null; georgeburgers.com is an expired/parked domain. Own-brand alternatives (restaurantji: no priced menu; UberEats and zmenu: bot-blocked to curl) did not turn up a second reachable source.
notes: Per house rule, DoorDash's 20% markup was not divided out and filed - George Burgers is specifically the documented example of that exact mistake, so its raw or corrected DoorDash numbers were not used either. Neither available source can be filed with confidence; needs either a dine-in artefact or a browser to reach UberEats/zmenu.

name: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka
notes: Replaced an earlier restaurantguru.com-sourced capture: the screener rejects directory sources like restaurantguru without an independent priced cross-check, and comparing it against this photo showed it was badly stale (restaurantguru's Salt Ramen $7.99 vs the board's current $9.50-$11.50 depending on size). This capture instead reads a dated, high-resolution in-store menu-board photograph hosted by restaurantji.com (a photo of the actual posted price board inside the restaurant, at Mitsuwa Marketplace) - the strongest evidence class available per house rules, cropped and zoomed with PowerShell to read each cell. Full Ramen Menu grid captured (Regular / Char Siu / Toroniku x Salt / Soy Sauce / Miso / Spicy Miso x Small/Medium/Large = all 36 combinations) and most of the Combination Menu grid (Combo sets A-E, each a ramen + a themed rice bowl, x flavor x size). The Miso row was skipped for B, C and D Combos only - obscured by camera glare in the photo, not missing from the menu; every other flavor row for those same combos (Salt, Soy Sauce, Spicy Miso) was fully legible and included. Side Dishes: only Rice ($1.50) and Charsiu Rice Bowl (Pork) ($4.50) were clearly legible; several other side dishes (green onion, kimchi-style, flavored egg, extra toroniku) were partially hidden behind a physical 'sold out' price tag stuck on the board and were not recorded. Cold Ramen Noodles ($15.95) is a seasonal item visible in the display case in the same photo set.

name: Sun Deck
notes: hoteldel.com embeds a first-party SinglePlatform widget for Sun Deck (data-location=sundeck) but it strips prices from every item except one ($34 Birria Nachos, a current Summer Special) - confirmed by fetching all three of its templates directly and stripping tags; unusable as a price source. Used a menuweb.menu-hosted PDF instead, parsed with pdftotext -raw (NOT -layout, which scrambled this multi-column menu into unpairable fragments). -raw preserved reliable single-token-per-line reading order and internally consistent name/price pairs (verified e.g. Mains section: Del Double Cheeseburger $29, Baja Striped Seabass $35, Braised Pork Bibimbap $33, Truffle short rib burger $48, San Diego Fish Sandwich $28 - each cleanly on its own line). Excluded 3 auto-generated SEO tag blocks that are not menu content ('Restaurant Category'->BAR, 'Ingredients Used'->SHRIMP, 'These Types Of Dishes Are Being Served'->BURGER/PANINI/FISH/SALAD). Dropped items published with no price at all: Fish Taco, Ceviche, Soft Drinks/Coke, a Mexican Dishes 'Tacos' entry, Chicken Sandwich, Beet Salad, an 'enhance your salad or bowl' upsell line, and the full still/red/white/sparkling wine-by-the-glass lists (wines on tap and bottles have no price in this source). The source appears to flatten Hotel Del's 3 separate Sun Deck menus (Main Menu, Cocktails/Wine/Beer Menu, Kids Menu) into many small same-theme sections (e.g. both 'Draft' and 'Draft Beers', both 'Bottle / Can' and 'Bottles / Cans') rather than one unified structure - recorded as the source presents it. Confidence medium: third-party auto-generated PDF aggregator, not the restaurant's own document, though price level ($11-$48, stated average $19.60) matches this beachfront hotel restaurant and pairings read as internally consistent.

name: Petes Place
blocked: Own domain (petesplacelamesa.com) is dead - redirects to a Network Solutions parking page. This is primarily a bar (Yelp/sagemenu/La Mesa Village Association all categorize it as Bars/restaurant-bar; the Village Association's own description of the business mentions only beers on tap, bottled beer and spirits, no food). Two directories that plausibly host a real food menu - m.zmenu.com and menupix.com - both returned a Cloudflare JS challenge to curl ('Just a moment...', no content). restaurantguru.com lists a 'Menu from owner (2 years ago)' but the page renders no priced items at all. sagemenu.com has no Menu tab, only gallery/reviews. restaurantji.com's only menu-tagged photo is a dated (Feb 2018) drink-specials chalkboard (Sunday Specials: $3.25 Miller High Life, $5 Peach Ciroc, etc.) - a snapshot, not a menu, and 8 years stale.
notes: Not marking not_found despite the drink-only-bar signals, because two searches turned up AI summaries claiming 'a bar food menu features classic favorites like burgers, wings, nachos' - unverified since both zmenu and menupix (the likely sources of that claim) were Cloudflare-blocked rather than confirmed empty. Needs a browser to get past the Cloudflare challenge on either site and settle whether a real priced food menu exists.

name: Cali's & Fries
blocked: Website is null; no first-party site. The restaurant's own ordering platforms (calisandfries.menu-res.com and calis-fries.res-menu.net) both return an empty JS shell to curl (5-byte chunked body, no server-rendered content) - need a browser. A menuweb.menu PDF exists but lists item NAMES with zero prices anywhere (22 items, 0 dollar signs in the extracted text) - unusable. That leaves two marketplace-owned sources: allmenus.com (which itself embeds Grubhub's own storefront - 'Grubhub.com Cali's & Fries... We make ordering easy') and foodboss.com (which embeds DoorDash/Postmates data). Per house rule these need an independent priced source to cross-check, so I compared them directly: every matching item differs by a clean, uniform ~1.143x ratio (Chips Plain $1.39 vs $1.59, Carne Asada Chips $6.99 vs $7.99, Carnitas Chips $6.99 vs $7.99, Shrimp Chips $7.75 vs $8.85, Chipotle/BBQ Chips $8.35 vs $9.55 - all landing on the same multiplier). That is disagreement, not corroboration: at least one of the two channels (likely both, by different amounts) carries a delivery markup, and a consistent ratio across a marketplace pair is itself a documented markup signature rather than confirmation of a true price.
notes: avoided calis-fries.weeblyte.com entirely - weeblyte.com is a barred fabricated-listing domain per house rule. No dine-in artefact (menu board photo, PDF with real prices) found. Needs either a browser (for menu-res.com/res-menu.net) or a genuinely independent priced source (not Grubhub- or DoorDash/Postmates-owned) to unblock.

name: Farmhouse 78
blocked: Toast server-side payload (window.__OO_STATE__, parsed by balancing braces) runs the menu query with respectAvailability:true, which time-gates the ENTIRE menu structure, not just what's rendered in the DOM. At capture time (~00:10 Pacific, Monday) the payload's paginatedMenuItems.groupings lists only two menus: COLD DRINKS (25 priced items: Soda Pop x9, Lemonade x3, Orange Juice x1, Kids Only x10, Milk x2) and HOT DRINKS (itemCount 0, empty right now). No Breakfast, Lunch, or Supper menu is present in the payload at all - this is a harder version of a documented prior finding for this exact restaurant, where a daytime capture got Lunch + Cold Drinks (64 items) because Breakfast (Fri-Sun 8-11) and Supper (Fri-Sat from 5) were simply the currently-non-serving dayparts. Right now even Lunch is absent, leaving only drinks.
notes: Not recording the 25 Cold Drinks items as a partial dishes list: they are real and unmarked-up, but filing them alone would misrepresent a mostly-food restaurant as a drinks-only one, which is worse than no capture. Needs a retry during actual trading hours (posted: Breakfast Fri-Sun 8-11am, Supper Fri-Sat from 5pm, presumably Lunch on other days/times) so the server-side respectAvailability filter includes the food menus.
